primary_semantics.summary: WHERE keeps true predicates. Unknown generally propagates, with decisive false-AND and true-OR exceptions. Empty-right IN/NOT IN gives false/true even for NULL. Otherwise a known match wins; an unmatched right NULL or NULL left operand gives unknown. EXISTS is Boolean row presence, independent of projected values. SQLite IS can match two NULLs.
An aggregate query without GROUP BY returns one result row even for zero input rows. The explicit ORDER BY clauses establish the row ordering used here.
COUNT(*) counts input rows; its value zero does not remove the aggregate result row.

q11_universal_proof.domain: Any finite multiset of INTEGER values or SQL NULL; left codes are exactly 7,9,NULL as given. Duplicate rows and the empty relation are allowed.
argument: Partition outer requests into code NULL and code a non-NULL integer x.
If the outer code is NULL, the left IS NOT NULL conjunct is false. NOT EXISTS is always a Boolean value, so the conjunction is false and the policy excludes the request.

If the outer code is a non-NULL integer x, the guard is true. The correlated WHERE b.code = x passes exactly right rows with the same non-NULL integer. NULL comparisons are unknown and do not pass WHERE.
EXISTS is true exactly when at least one such matching row exists. Negating it is therefore true exactly when no equal blocked row exists, which is the required absence clause.

Adding duplicates changes neither whether a matching row exists nor the outer known-code guard. For an empty right relation no row matches and every known request is retained while the NULL request remains excluded. These cases exhaust the stated domain.

counterexamples.reason: Filtering an already empty relation leaves it empty; NULL NOT IN empty is true.
There is no row for the equality predicate to match; NOT EXISTS is true, and no outer known-code guard exists.
No blocked integer equals 9, yet the NULL right row makes nonmembership unknown; WHERE excludes it.

q11_universal_proof.finite_worksheet_limit: The four named scenarios demonstrate results and counterexamples. The partition-and-existence argument, not those examples alone, establishes the universal policy.
